- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed — leading to over-forecasted peaks; apply lagged smoothing or dampen momentum.
- In periods of high volatility or sharp price moves, model tends to misjudge mean reversion; use recent 7-day average as anchor for correction.
- If sentiment is consistently low or flat, model often underestimates true price range; increase forecast baseline by 2–5% to account for suppressed sentiment.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-period corrections — especially after strong upward moves — so add a 1–3 day downward bias in final 5–7 days of forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model may lag in adjusting — apply early correction to first 3–5 days of forecast to reflect sentiment change.
